projects.name: AI Tray
projects.tagline: Native desktop companion for Claude Code and GitHub Copilot usage
projects.description: AI Tray is a native desktop companion for Claude Code and GitHub Copilot subscription usage (macOS menu bar / Windows system tray), with provider dashboards, session and week rings, diagnostics, and settings.

showcase.problem: Tracking Claude Code and Copilot subscription usage usually means leaving your flow for a browser or CLI — and Windows/macOS tray experiences are inconsistent.
showcase.solution: A lightweight Flutter tray app that surfaces provider health, session/week usage rings, diagnostics, and settings from the menu bar or system tray.

features.title: Multi-provider usage
features.description: Claude Code (stable) and GitHub Copilot (experimental) dashboards.

features.title: Tray rings
features.description: Live, cached, refreshing, and error states in the menu bar / tray.

features.title: Diagnostics and logs
features.description: In-app diagnostics and log views for support and dogfood.

demo.note: Install from GitHub Releases (macOS arm64 / Windows x64). No public web embed.

media.caption: Claude dashboard with session / week rings

showcase.architecture: Flutter desktop app under ai_tray/ with Riverpod state, tray_manager / window_manager, and provider-specific usage pipelines (Claude CLI, Copilot sidecar).
showcase.installation: Download macOS arm64 or Windows x64 builds from GitHub Releases, or run from source: cd ai_tray && flutter run -d macos

changelog.notes: Claude usage parsing fix for missing session reset suffix; macOS arm64 + Windows x64 release pipeline.

showcase.contributing: Ideas for tray actions and provider adapters are welcome via GitHub issues.

projects.name: Document Platform
projects.tagline: Flutter-native document editing you can embed
projects.description: Document Platform is an independent Flutter document-editing stack: schema-driven model, commands, hybrid rendering, clipboard/HTML interchange, plugins, and templates — split into focused Melos packages hosts can compose without forking a monolith.

showcase.problem: Enterprise Flutter apps need structured rich documents, selection/IME, toolbar, and clipboard fidelity — without bolting those concerns onto an editor that was not designed for embedding.
showcase.solution: A Melos package monorepo with clear dependency direction toward document_core: model, session, presentation, UI, interchange, plugins, and theming that hosts compose.

features.title: Schema-driven document model
features.description: Hierarchical nodes, attributions, and transactional mutations in document_core.

features.title: Editor session & commands
features.description: Selection, IME, inverse undo/redo, and command pipeline in document_editor.

features.title: Interchange fidelity
features.description: Clipboard pipeline plus HTML and Markdown packages for host integration.

features.title: Embeddable examples
features.description: example_basic, example_embed, example_enterprise, and email_template_editor showcase hosts.

demo.note: Run examples/example_basic locally (Editor Playground). Interactive web embed for the public portal is planned.

media.caption: Hosts compose packages; dependencies point inward toward document_core

showcase.architecture: Dependency direction is inward toward document_core. Layers: model → session → presentation → UI → interchange → plugins/theme. Cycles require an ADR. See docs/architecture/.

architectureDiagram.caption: Model, session, rendering, widgets, interchange, plugins

platformSupport.notes: Supported for portal and host embeds

showcase.installation: Clone https://github.com/roshandroids/Document_Platform, run dart pub get at the workspace root, then: cd examples/example_basic && flutter run -d macos

changelog.notes: Directional architecture freeze closeout; package suite at 0.1.0 with high coverage gates.

showcase.contributing: See CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/process/ in this repository. Prefer package-level changes with ADRs when dependency direction is affected.

projects.name: Localization Analyzer
projects.tagline: Find missing, unused, and hardcoded localization issues
projects.description: Pure-Dart localization analysis engine that scans Dart sources and ARB files for hardcoded text, missing keys, unused keys, and duplicates — with no Flutter or DevTools UI dependencies. Frontends (CLI, DevTools) only read files and present diagnostics.

showcase.problem: Localization drift—hardcoded strings, missing keys, unused entries, and duplicates—often appears only after QA or production releases.
showcase.solution: A Pure-Dart analyzer API that frontends call with source and ARB inputs to surface diagnostics early in the development loop.

features.title: Hardcoded text detection
features.description: Flag string literals that look like UI copy, with // loc-ignore suppressions.

features.title: Missing and unused keys
features.description: Compare Dart usage against ARB definitions across locales.

features.title: Allowlist configuration
features.description: Ignore exact strings, patterns, and path substrings via AnalyzerConfig or JSON.

demo.note: Run the workspace CLI (dart run tool/scan_localization.dart). Public interactive demo not published.

showcase.architecture: Pure-Dart package with no Flutter/DevTools dependencies. Hosts (CLI, DevTools) load files and present LocalizationAnalyzer results.
showcase.installation: Use from the MBO / cmic_localization_inspector workspace: depend on packages/localization_analyzer, or run dart run tool/scan_localization.dart from the workspace root.

changelog.notes: Analyzer API with hardcoded/missing/unused/duplicate diagnostics and allowlist config.

showcase.contributing: Report false positives and locale edge cases via GitHub issues on the MBO repository.
